the_ruling_verbatim: sigh. the point behind having you read that was because it lays out what the layers are for. you wrote that based on the INTENDED state of the system at that time. Which is most of a month ago. so the question is: if we're building those components, and we have a skill that connects them together, they don't all have to be built out just to build the holders. what has to happen is starting with orientation, we build out everything we can now. and then keep improving it. orientation will add a json packet to the ticket, constrain will add to that. survey will add to that. those can be completely deterministic. and ONCE THEY WORK we can start working on the other ones later. WHY: The goal is not to reduce token spend for you. you are cached. but as we build out decompose, it will start off by failing over to Hex (our apple m1 studio 32g hostname: hex or hex.local) and hex will deposit graph tree nodes that will allow decompose to solve that problem. and when the next one comes along, it'll learn more. and you'll still be doing the builds. so you can score the quality of the information downward just by doing more tool calls before the build is done. the system learns from you.
now_the_spec_says: Not token spend — Claude is cached. Uncompiled preamble passes fail over to Hex (hex.local), which deposits tree nodes so the pass answers the next one itself. Claude keeps doing the builds and is the ground truth: packet quality is scored downward by tool calls before done.
the_reason_that_dies: TOKEN SPEND AS THE WHY OF COMPILING THE PREAMBLE. It came from Akien's own 2026-07-19 paper (~/.akien/20260719.PreBuildPacketDesignPattern.md), whose economics section is explicit — the preamble is 're-derived only because nobody handed it the answers', triage is 'the starvation gate', a measured ~89% token cut. That paper stands as what it is: a clean-room design pattern written against the INTENDED state of a month ago, and it is not edited by this ruling (it is not even in a repo). What dies is CC treating its economics as this system's motive. 'The goal is not to reduce token spend for you. you are cached.' The compiling is for LEARNING: a pass that answers from its own tree has knowledge, and a pass that is merely cheap has a discount.
the_ladder_this_names: THE STRATA GAIN A RUNG AND CHANGE HANDS. The chain has been documented as three strata tried cheapest-first — deterministic floor, then the nexus's graph tree, then the CLAUDE CEILING. This ruling puts HEX (the Apple M1 Studio, 32G, hostname hex / hex.local) in the ceiling for the preamble: 'as we build out decompose, it will start off by failing over to Hex and hex will deposit graph tree nodes that will allow decompose to solve that problem. and when the next one comes along, it'll learn more.' So the ceiling is not a permanent tenant but a DEPOSITOR — every failover leaves the tree better than it found it, which is what makes the rung below fill. Claude's place moves rather than shrinks: 'and you'll still be doing the builds.'
the_measurement_it_names: PACKET QUALITY IS SCORED BY TOOL-CALL VOLUME TO DONE, and it is scored DOWNWARD: 'you can score the quality of the information downward just by doing more tool calls before the build is done. the system learns from you.' The builder is the instrument. If the packet was good the build needs few calls; if it was thin the builder goes looking, and the looking is the measurement. This supersedes CC's design of the same morning, which had the build's tool calls producing PER-CLAIM FALSIFICATIONS — each finding naming the berth field it contradicted, plus an unsolved question about what counts as a contradiction and how to avoid a firehose. A score has no firehose because it classifies nothing. Recorded as a correction on ticket the-builds-tool-calls-are-evidence-about-the-chart (appended, not rewritten — Law 7).
the_build_order_it_names: HOLDERS FIRST, CONTENTS ONE AT A TIME, and the sequencing is his: 'they don't all have to be built out just to build the holders. what has to happen is starting with orientation, we build out everything we can now. and then keep improving it. orientation will add a json packet to the ticket, constrain will add to that. survey will add to that. those can be completely deterministic. and ONCE THEY WORK we can start working on the other ones later.' Three consequences CC must not blur: the packet ACCUMULATES on the ticket rather than each stage emitting a separate artifact; orient/constrain/survey are the deterministic three and are named as capable of being COMPLETELY so; and the remaining four wait on those three WORKING, which is a gate on evidence and not a schedule.
measured_by_cc_2026_08_14: CC's measurement, labelled as CC's. The dial over 284 berthed packets reads the three named-deterministic passes as the LEAST compiled of the seven: orient floor 0.40, constrain 0.25, survey 0.20 (against 0.33 for decompose/triage/hypothesize/validate). And the tree stratum reads 0.00 on ALL SEVEN nexi across all 284 packets — the middle rung, which is exactly where Hex's deposits are supposed to land, is contributing nothing today. That is a measurement of the corpus, not a claim about the ruling; it says the ladder this ruling describes currently has an empty rung, which is a thing to know before Hex starts depositing into it.
